records.issue_text: [BUG] The modified BasePaginator.get_result unclamps offsets when cursor.is_prev, so any client-crafted cursor carrying a negative offset produces a negative slice on every existing paginator (DateTimePaginator included), which Django rejects. Any user of any DateTimePaginator-based endpoint can send a cursor with is_prev=true and negative offset and crash the request with a ValueError/500 — a regression on all endpoints sharing BasePaginator, not just audit logs.
records.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result`, the new logic explicitly avoids clamping when `cursor.is_prev` is true: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Since `offset` comes from `cursor.offset` (see `Cursor.__init__`: `self.offset = int(offset)`), a client-crafted cursor with a negative offset and `is_prev=true` will produce a negative queryset slice. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and will raise an exception, turning this into a request crash/500. This impacts any endpoint using paginators that rely on

records.issue_text: [BUG] The prev-page dedup branch checks `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` but results were sliced starting at start_offset (possibly negative), so the length comparison against the unadjusted offset is wrong for the negative-offset path. On backward pagination with negative offsets, the last result is not trimmed when it should be, or is trimmed when it shouldn't be, yielding duplicated/missing rows at page boundaries.
records.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the “trim last element” condition is `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:`. But the query is sliced as `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` (both in the normal and negative-offset branches). That slice can return at most `limit + extra` items (i.e., `stop - start_offset`), not `offset + limit + extra`. When `cursor.offset` is nonzero (and especially when negative in the advanced path), `offset + limit + extra` won’t match `len(results)` even when the slice is “full”, so the trimming logic will be skipped/ap

records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the key attribute, which raises TypeError when the paginator is used with datetime ordering (the audit log endpoint orders by -datetime), since datetime objects support neither __floor__ nor numeric comparison to ints. The first request through the optimized path (any superuser with optimized_pagination=true) crashes in get_item_key during build_cursor, returning a 500 — the feature has no working configuration at all, and the unit-looking copy from OffsetPaginator's int-key logic was never adapted for DateTimePaginator's data type.
records.rationale: In the optimized path, the audit log endpoint paginates with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `order_by="-datetime"` (organization_auditlogs.py). `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` then `math.floor/ceil(value)` and casts to `int` (paginator.py). If `self.key` corresponds to the ordered field (`datetime`), `value` will be a datetime object and `math.floor/ceil` will raise `TypeError`, causing a 500 during cursor building (`build_cursor(... key=self.get_item_key ...)`).

When enable_advanced_features is on and the client follows a 'prev' cursor (cursor.is_prev with results), get_result calls get_item_key(results[0], for_prev=True) and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the previous page of audit logs.
records.rationale: In the optimized path, the audit log endpoint paginates with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `order_by="-datetime"` (organization_auditlogs.py). `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` then `math.floor/ceil(value)` and casts to `int` (paginator.py). If `self.key` corresponds to the ordered field (`datetime`), `value` will be a datetime object and `math.floor/ceil` will raise `TypeError`, causing a 500 during cursor building (`build_cursor(... key=self.get_item_key ...)`).

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The prev-dedup logic compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra using the raw (possibly negative) offset while the slice used start_offset, so the two offsets disagree and the boundary-trim branch results[:-1] silently drops the wrong element or never fires. Admins paging backwards through audit logs on the optimized path get a duplicated or missing row at page boundaries — silent data mispagination rather than a crash, and the drift between the two offset computations makes the next change to this paginator harder to reason about.
records.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the “trim last element” condition is `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:`. But the query is sliced as `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` (both in the normal and negative-offset branches). That slice can return at most `limit + extra` items (i.e., `stop - start_offset`), not `offset + limit + extra`. When `cursor.offset` is nonzero (and especially when negative in the advanced path), `offset + limit + extra` won’t match `len(results)` even when the slice is “full”, so the trimming logic will be skipped/ap

records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewrite of OffsetPaginator.get_result clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursors, silently changing behavior, while the prev-cursor dedup check still compares len(results) against the unclamped `offset`. A forward cursor with a negative offset previously (in the old code) produced a Django slicing error surfaced as a 500; now it silently returns the first page of the dataset — the client believes it received page N but gets page 1 with no error, a silent-partial-success desync. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually false and is the load-bearing justification for the whole feature. The next maintainer who reads this comment will extend the negative-offset path (e.g. to the OffsetPaginator branch above, which was already partially rewired for it) trusting a claim the ORM violates; this is the exact comment that hides the P0 ValueError above from a future reviewer.

records.issue_text: [BUG] When cursor is None the paginator synthesizes Cursor(0, 0, 0), but when a client supplies a cursor whose value is 0 or unparseable, cursor_value falls back to 0 and build_queryset(0, ...) filters against a fabricated boundary value. A malformed or zero-valued cursor from the optimized path filters the queryset with key <= 0 (or >= 0 depending on direction) instead of rejecting the cursor, silently returning an empty or wrong page with HTTP 200 — the API reports success while the client's requested position is dropped.
